instruments.evidence: 92b19d6c7: RegisterRequest and LoginRequest gain login_key (and salt, rounds); auth_login_key.go adds registrationCredentials, validateLoginKey, PreLogin, placeholderSalt and MoveToLoginKey; UpgradeToLoginKey in models, ports, the Postgres wrapper and the mock; Create writes the scheme.

The handlers bind these request structs directly, so the new JSON fields (login_key, kdf_salt, kdf_iterations) reach the service today; the pre-login and move endpoints arrive in K1b-2.
Read the rows back after each write in the models test: after the move, scheme 2 and the new key copy; after a password write, scheme 1 with salt and rounds NULL.
MinKDFIterations (600000) matches users_auth_scheme_check; the salt size bounds match what PreLogin returns (16 bytes for a missing name).
PreLoginResponse carries scheme, kdf_salt, kdf_iterations: exactly what the app needs to derive the login key.
The rule 'scheme 2 signs in only with its key' lives once, in Login; the OmniGame runtime login calls the same Login, so it inherits the rule.
The new UpgradeToLoginKey parameter is carried by all three implementations; go build ./... and go vet ./... pass on the whole backend.
The mock mirrors the SQL: moves once, clears salt on a password write, replaces the key copy; the models test checks the real SQL does the same.
Login keys in tests are 32 random-looking bytes in base64, as the app will send; salts are 16 bytes.
Checked; nothing new.

Refused: a 31-byte key, a non-base64 key, an 8-byte salt, 599999 and 10000001 rounds, a key with a password, a password to a scheme 2 account, a key to a scheme 1 account, a second move, a move with the wrong password.
Boundaries: exactly 600000 rounds and a 16-byte salt are accepted; one below is refused.

Every writer of password_hash: the reset handler (auth.go:636) and change-password (users.go:1165) call UpdatePassword with a bcrypt of the raw password, which left scheme 2 in place (finding k1b-password-write-keeps-scheme). Account deletion and data export compare the raw password and so refuse scheme 2 accounts: they fail closed until phase K2 moves them.
The 'wrong kind of secret' branch is reached by each case in TestSchemeTwoSignsInOnlyWithItsLoginKey.
Every refusal returns the same 'invalid username or password' and is logged with the scheme, not the secret.
PreLogin gives banned and deleted accounts the placeholder answer, as Login refuses them.
The KDF bounds live once in auth_login_key.go.
Other places that store a private key copy: UpdateEncryptedPrivateKey (the app's own upload) is unchanged; the move now replaces the copy itself.
No shared state; the move is guarded by WHERE auth_scheme = 1, so two concurrent moves cannot both succeed.

instruments.why: Each write is one UPDATE; no multi-step transaction.
